missed_subsystems: CI/CD pipeline — GitHub Actions workflows that run on push/pull_request, install deps, stand up MongoDB and start the app; a real automation/supply-chain trust boundary absent from recon (.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml, .github/workflows/lint.yml; also .travis.yml, Gruntfile.js)

PaaS/Heroku deploy surface — deploy descriptor exposing MONGODB_URI ('must be publicly accessible') plus a postdeploy db-reset, and the process manager start command, none reflected in recon (app.json, Procfile)
notes: Recon was compared line-by-line against the actual repo tree and source. The core application attack surface is captured accurately and completely: all HTTP entry points in app/routes/index.js are present (E1-E14), including the SSRF route (note recon labels E12 'GET /research?url=&symbol=' — the route is registered as GET /research with isLoggedIn, and the url+symbol SSRF sink lives inside research.js displayResearch, not in the route table; functionally covered). The 12 tutorial sub-pages (a1-a10, redos, ssrf in app/routes/tutorial.js) collapse into recon's E13. All data stores (Mongo users/allocations/contributions/memos/counters, in-memory session store, committed TLS key+cert, plaintext seed creds in artifacts/db-reset.js) match D1-D8. Trust boundaries TB1-TB6 match (plaintext HTTP, anon/auth, user/admin with /benefits missing isAdmin per index.js lines 55-60, app->Mongo, SSRF egress, container/host). External deps X1-X8 cover the security-relevant packages. DAO note: app/data/research-dao.js exists but is a dead stub (getBySymbol defines an unused inner function, no DB access); its omission from recon hides no risk since the SSRF is in the route. Genuine gaps: (1) CI/CD — two GitHub Actions workflows (and .travis.yml/Gruntfile) are a real subsystem/automation trust boundary entirely absent; e2e-test.yml sets persist-credentials:false (good) but the pipeline is unrepresented. (2) PaaS deploy config (app.json declaring a publicly accessible MONGODB_URI + postdeploy db-reset, and Procfile's forever launcher) is missing. Minor: config/env/development.js injects a livereload <script> via environmentalScripts (dev only). None of these hide a core application-layer OWASP vulnerability, so the coverage denominator is sound for the app itself, but the CI/CD subsystem is a legitimate category-level miss.
